title: Canary resilience lab journal and traffic morphology (wip)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working lab journal for thinking about canary resilience when traffic shape mutates unexpectedly. Focus is on: (1) classes of traffic morphologies we see in the wild, (2) simple operational checks and lightweight probes to detect brittle canaries early, (3) rapid rollback and containment patterns that minimize blast radius while preserving signal, and (4) cross-functional comms/ownership checklist for multi-team activations.

Audience and context:
- Primary: release stewards, experiment owners, SRE on-call, product PMs who run multi-model rollouts.
- Context: complements the staged-rollout playbooks — this file emphasizes dynamic traffic shapes (seasonal spikes, bot floods, query storms from partner integrations) rather than feature deltas.

High-level taxonomy: traffic morphologies (quick reference)
- Baseline steady: low variance, typical for internal tools and narrow cohorts. Canary pass/fail thresholds should be tight.
- Diurnal amplifiers: predictable daily rhythm; latency budgets should be matched to peak windows.
- Burst frontloads: short, very high qps bursts (cron jobs, nightly syncs). Need burst-tolerant routing and token-bucket headroom.
- Heavy tail requests: a small fraction of requests cause long tails (large context lengths, rare reranking tasks). Track tail p50/p95/p99 separately.
- Correlated noise: many simultaneous requests similar in content (e.g., marketing email hits)—causes KV cache warm/cold artifacts.
- Synthetic/traffic-replay: replayed sessions from QA or partners produce unnatural sequence lengths or repeated prompts.

Canary brittleness vectors to watch
- Model variant mismatch with seqlen distribution: quantized small-model optimized for short contexts will spike CPU/GPU when it receives long sequences.
- Tokenization edge-cases: new user input patterns causing exponential decoding loops (rare but catastrophic).
- Cache churn: prefix cache thrash when similar queries flood different shards.
- Backpressure cascade: slow downstream (DB or external scoring) increases request duration and causes autoscaler chase.

Quick operational heuristics (pre-flight checks)
- Synthetic probe matrix: generate 6 probe-types that reflect morphologies above and run them against canary and control for 10 minutes pre-activation. Compare p50/p95/p99 + cost-per-token delta.
- Warmup window: activate canary at 1% for 15m with real traffic + synthetic probes. Verify latency and error envelopes; check for amplification of error by gateway.
- Resource headroom check: ensure GPU mem/cpu usage < 70% for canary worker pool on probe workload. If >70% abort rollout.
- Tokenization fuzz test: run corpus of new user inputs (from prior 24h) through canary tokenizer and check for unusually long token counts.
- KV/cache key uniqueness: sample 1k recent requests and estimate cache hit ratio on canary variant. If hit ratio < historical baseline -20% then escalate.

Traffic partitioning and morphing patterns (practical snippets)
- Micro-slices: prefer many small, diverse slices rather than single large slice. Example split: 0.5% power-users, 0.5% new-accounts, 0.5% mobile-android, 0.5% partner-api. Rotate slices every 2 hours to detect slow drift.
- Temporal ramping: ramp exponential in two stages: (a) 0.5%->2% over 30m, (b) 2%->10% over next 60m; interleave synthetic stress probes at each step.
- Shock absorber capacity: reserve a small pool of dedicated capacity for automatic fallback traffic when canary drops beyond thresholds. Routing policy: route 100% of fallback to stable pool until canary recovers.

Signals to watch (fast-fail and slow-degrade)
- Fast-fail (minutes): increase in 5xx errors, sudden p99 spike > 2x baseline, tokenization exceptions, GPU OOM, autoscaler rapid scale-up.
- Slow-degrade (hours): sustained p95 increase, model quality drift (LLM eval on sample prompts shows BLEU-like/ML-acceptable drop), user retention signal down in cohort analysis.

Containment and rollback playbook (ops checklist)
- Immediate (t=0–3m): cut canary to 0% (via routing plane), undo any feature flags tied to model difference, open incident channel #canary-responses.
- Short (t=3–30m): snapshot canary logs + tracer dumps to S3, gather synthetic probe results, collect kernel/GPU metrics. Notify stakeholders (oncall, experiment owner, eng lead, product PM).
- Recovery (t=30m–4hr): if root cause is clear and fix small (config, threshold), consider rolling restart + 0.5% steady smoke test. If unknown, keep canary offline until postmortem.

Cross-functional run roles (one-line owner responsibilities)
- Release steward: orchestrates ramping cadence + final go/no-go call.
- Experiment owner / PM: owns hypothesis and acceptance criteria, communicates user-facing risks.
- SRE/operator: watch system signals, execute rollback and capacity actions.
- Model owner / Applied ML: interprets quality regressions and advises model fallbacks.
- Data/infra partner: if partner integrations generate heavy-tail, coordinate traffic gating.

Templates and quick artifacts (copy/paste)
- Activation quick-check (to paste into activation slack):
  - Stamp: [UTC time]
  - Canary build: vX.Y.Z
  - Ramp plan: 0.5->2->10 over 90m + synthetic probes
  - Fast-fail triggers: p99>2x, 5xx rate>0.5% absolute, GPU mem>85%
  - Owner: Aisha Malik (release steward) + oncall SRE

- Post-activation postmortem skeleton (fields): hypothesis, timeline, metrics snapshot, root cause, mitigation, followups, responsible.

Open questions / research experiments to run
- How often should we rotate micro-slices to maximize early detection without burning noise? A/B test rotation cadence.
- Can we build a compact synthetic probe generator that emulates query bloom behavior with <1% additional cost? (idea: delta-fuzz on top-1000 recent queries)
- Evaluate model fallback cost tradeoffs: steady fallback to smaller quantized models vs partial rerank hybrid. Need cost curve and quality drop metrics.

Notes to self and TODOs (short)
- (TODO) Wire synthetic probe runner into the Console -> show probe health on activation page (EPIC: CON-452).
- (TODO) Add traffic-morphology selector to canary templates (dropdown: burst|correlated|heavy-tail|steady).
- (Followup) Run 3 replay experiments simulating partner replays with varied seqlen distributions next sprint. Assign: Jonas.

Appendix: quick checklist for oncall when observing canary instability
1) Toggle canary to 0% immediately.
2) Check GPU OOMs and autoscaler events.
3) Run tokenization fuzz on last 1k requests.
4) Upload traces and mark incident.
5) If rate-limited downstream is root cause, throttle partner queues and re-run 15m smoke.

End of journal entry. This is a scratchpad — expect updates after next lab runs.
